from pagination import paginate


def test_page_two_size_two_returns_three_four():
    result = paginate(list(range(1, 8)), 2, 2)
    assert result == [3, 4]
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_page_numbers_are_one_based():
    assert paginate(list(range(1, 8)), 1, 2) == [1, 2]
    assert paginate(list(range(1, 8)), 2, 2) == [3, 4]
    assert paginate(list(range(1, 8)), 3, 2) == [5, 6]


def test_empty_input_returns_empty_list():
    result = paginate([], 1, 2)
    assert result == []
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_invalid_page_returns_empty_list():
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], 0, 2) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], -1, 2) == []


def test_invalid_page_size_returns_empty_list():
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], 1, 0) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2, 3], 1, -2) == []


def test_page_beyond_last_page_returns_empty_list():
    result = paginate(list(range(1, 8)), 10, 2)
    assert result == []
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_last_partial_page_returns_remaining_items():
    assert paginate(list(range(1, 8)), 4, 2) == [7]


def test_first_page_returns_first_size_items():
    assert paginate(list(range(1, 8)), 1, 3) == [1, 2, 3]

patches.rationale: The original paginate used zero-based indexing (start = page * page_size), so page 2 returned range(3,5) instead of [3,4]. The fix makes page numbers one-based by computing start = (page - 1) * page_size. Slicing a range returns a range object, so the new regression tests must compare against list(...) or use list inputs to assert the exact list result. I use list(range(1,8)) as the input so the returned slice is a list, matching the issue's expected [3,4] value and type. Empty/invalid inputs still return [] and pages beyond the last page yield an empty slice.
